details: package.json declares zero dependencies and zero devDependencies; there is no lockfile and none is required. npm audit correctly refuses (ENOLOCK).
No go.mod / pubspec.yaml / requirements.txt / Cargo.toml. Repository is 26 shell + 25 bats + 135 json + 52 md files with no third-party runtime code.
Attack surface is the shell hooks themselves, which this audit targets directly.

findings.issue: Shell-metacharacter welding: the hook's word boundary is literal whitespace only, the shell's is whitespace + metacharacters + IFS. Both the F65 control-plane gate and Layer 1/2 fall to it, and the result is `allow` (auto-approved, no prompt) — not a fallthrough.
findings.root_cause: Three places share one wrong model of what ends a word. (1) __tokenize_segment() ends a token only on ' ' or TAB (:1504). (2) normalize_path_token() strips only quotes and backslashes (:852) — it never strips '>', '<', '(' or ')'. (3) scan_control_plane_delete() segments on `tr ';|&'` (:1588), three of the shell's metacharacters. The real shell also terminates a word at '>', '>>', '<', '>&', '(' and ')', and re-splits unquoted expansions on $IFS. Layer 1/2 have the identical defect for a different reason: BLOCKED's trailing anchor is `( |$|[;&|])` (:90) and INDIRECT_PATTERNS' eval anchors are `^eval\b` / `[;&|] *eval\b` (:127-128) — '>' and ')' are in neither character class.
sub_mechanisms: (a) verb welded to a PRECEDING metacharacter defeats arming: `(rm -rf .claude)` tokenizes as `(rm`, which matches neither `rm` nor `*/rm` at :1566, so armed stays 0 and the operand loop never runs.

(b) operand welded to a FOLLOWING metacharacter defeats the path match: `rm -rf .claude>/dev/null` tokenizes as `.claude>/dev/null`, which matches none of the case arms at :1167-1211 (it is not `.claude`, not `.claude/*`, has no glob character).
findings.oracle: Six representative payloads re-executed against a real .claude tree: `rm -rf .claude>/dev/null`, `(rm -rf .claude)`, `cat <(rm -rf .claude)`, `true && (rm -rf .claude)`, `rm -rf .claude/hooks>/dev/null`, `rm -rf .claude>out.txt` — DELETED under /bin/bash AND /bin/zsh, 6/6 both shells. The $IFS variants DELETED under bash, INTACT under zsh (zsh does not word-split unquoted expansions by default). `rm -rf .claude<x` is decided allow but aborts when x is absent, so it is listed for completeness only.
findings.impact: The two highest-value targets are fully exposed: the .claude directory itself (gitignored, absent from PROTECTED_GLOBS — permanent loss, no detection, no recovery) and ~/.claude/plugins/cc-harness (the installed plugin, i.e. this firewall). Deleting the latter removes the control that is supposed to prevent it. `(eval "rm -rf /")` additionally shows the deny tier's eval anchors are position-anchored to separators the shell does not require.
findings.not_a_regression: Identical decisions at dec9293, 978d8f2, cc71ce8 and 1c6c1db. Pre-existing across the whole F65 cycle, not introduced by any of the last six rounds.
findings.not_in_any_declared_residual: Checked every axis in progress/contracts/sprint-51.json open_axes_2026_08_04: operand_before_verb_ordering (verb here precedes the operand normally), verb_via_substitution (verb is a literal ordinary word, no substitution, no encoding), scope_note (no parameter expansion in the '>' and '(' forms), indirect_operand (operand is a literal in the command string), cwd_shift (no cd), unenumerated_verbs (rm/rmdir/mv are all enumerated). None applies.
findings.controls_that_still_hold: rm -rf .claude / rm -rf .claude/ / rm -rf .clau* / find .claude -delete / { rm -rf .claude;} / rm -rf .claude; / rm -rf .claude& / rm -rf .claude|true -> all ask. rm .claude/settings.json>/dev/null and (rm .claude/settings.local.json) -> ask, because the named-file ASK arms carry no trailing anchor; that coverage does NOT extend to the .claude directory, .claude/hooks or .claude/plugins.
findings.no_friction_baseline_for_a_fix: A fix must keep these allow: `rm -rf dist>/dev/null`, `(rm -rf node_modules)`, `cat <(ls)`, `ls $(pwd)`, `echo $(date)`.
findings.remediation_direction: Do not enumerate more path notations — that is the failure mode this file has hit for sixteen rounds. Make the hook's word boundary the shell's word boundary: treat unquoted '>', '<', '(', ')', ';', '&', '|' as token terminators inside __tokenize_segment() (and let the segment splitter see the same set), and replace Layer 1/2's `( |$|[;&|])` trailing class with a general not-a-path-character class. The property to assert is falsifiable and already has a harness: the 12th round built an argv oracle — assert that the hook's tokenization agrees with the real shell's argv for generated payloads, rather than adding case-by-case tests.

findings.issue: Over-ask regression introduced during this F65 cycle: any command containing an UNQUOTED command substitution that itself contains ';', '|' or '&' is asked unconditionally, even when no delete verb and no control-plane path is present anywhere.
findings.root_cause: scan_control_plane_delete() splits on `tr ';|&'` (:1588) BEFORE tokenizing, which cuts `$( ... | ... )` in half. __skip_dollar_paren() then scans to end of segment without finding the close paren, returns __OPAQUE_END=-1 (:1304), and :1543 raises SEGMENT_UNSAFE -> ask. The fail-closed reflex is right in principle; the defect is that the imbalance is manufactured by the hook's own pre-split, not present in the input.
measured: npm run build && echo $(date +%s | tail -c4) -> ask
findings.regression_proof: dec9293 decides `echo $(ls | wc -l)` allow; 978d8f2, cc71ce8 and 1c6c1db all decide ask. Introduced by the 12th-verdict commit (978d8f2) that started treating command substitutions in __tokenize_segment().
findings.why_existing_tests_miss_it: The 12th verdict added exactly two over-blocking regression tests — `ls $(pwd)` and a backtick inside a quoted commit message — and both still pass, because neither contains a separator INSIDE the substitution. `echo "count: $(ls -1 | wc -l)"` also passes, because NORMALIZED_CMD neutralises the pipe inside the double quotes. The uncovered shape is the common one: an unquoted substitution with a pipe.
findings.security_relevance: This is the same over-blocking failure the 12th verdict rejected, re-entering through a different door. Routine ask prompts on read-only commands train reflexive approval, and the ask tier's entire value rests on the user still reading it.

findings.issue: Confirmation, not a new finding: unbraced `$Z` splitting a verb inside a substitution is open. `echo `r$Zm -rf .claude`` -> allow. __strip_dollar_brace() only recognises `${...}`, so `$Z` is never removed and the adjacent literals never join into `rm`.
findings.status: WITHIN the declared residual. Commit 1c6c1db restated verb_via_substitution.remaining_gap at mechanism level — 'every case where erasing does not expose an adjacent literal verb word' — and this payload is inside that set. Reported only to confirm the restatement's coverage is accurate rather than example-shaped; no action requested.

findings.issue: Question 3 answered: the single-source structure is real, and both consumers do read it. Enumerated every reference — L1348 (__scan_opaque_verb_matches iterates both arrays), L1556 (scan_control_plane_delete reads ARM_DELETE_VERB_DELETE_GATED in the -delete branch), L1565 (scan_control_plane_delete iterates ARM_DELETE_VERBS_UNCONDITIONAL). The only other textual verb enumerations in the file are comments at L829 and L1593. No duplicated live list exists; the 13th verdict's fix holds.
findings.caveat: Same list, different matching semantics. The token consumer matches AFTER normalize_path_token() with `== verb || == */verb`, so `/bin/rm` arms. The span consumer matches with a word-boundary regex on raw and stripped copies. Both directions are more permissive at finding verbs, so the asymmetry opens no gap — but the comment at :1307-1312 slightly overstates it as full equivalence. Also: the arrays are plain globals, not readonly; no code path can assign them, so this is documentation-level only.

findings.issue: Question 5 answered: no self-referencing `local` traps remain. An automated scan of every local/declare/typeset statement found zero cases where a variable assigned earlier in the SAME statement is dereferenced later in it. All nine sites where a later `local` legitimately uses an earlier one — L897 (__brace_range_value), L922 (__brace_range_info), L958 (__brace_prescan), L989 (__brace_find_group), L1032 (__brace_split_top_level), L1270 (__skip_backtick), L1292 (__skip_dollar_paren), L1367 (__strip_dollar_brace), L1443 (__tokenize_segment) — are correctly split into separate statements. The 7th- and 12th-verdict class is closed.

Question 2 answered: the .claude/ recovery-plane claim is factually correct and correctly recorded. What is NOT earned is the conclusion the docs draw from it — docs/INVARIANTS.md:701 treats prediction as the control that covers this path, and AUDIT-1 shows the prediction gate does not hold for the plainest notations. Recommend the threat model state the residual as measured, not as covered. Note the asymmetry that hooks/hooks.json IS tracked and IS in PROTECTED_GLOBS (recovery exists), while .claude/** has neither prediction (per AUDIT-1) nor detection nor recovery.

Question 4 answered: the designed division of labour between Layer 2 and the F65 gate matches the code and was verified by measurement. Caveat worth recording — the two halves are kept in sync by hand. INDIRECT_PATTERNS hardcodes `(rm|chmod|chown|mkfs|eval)` at :131 and :133 with no reference to ARM_DELETE_VERBS_UNCONDITIONAL. Adding a verb to the F65 array does not add it to Layer 2, and vice versa. Not a live gap — the union currently covers the intent — but it is the same 'prose claim of parity with no mechanism' the 13th verdict rejected inside F65, now living one layer up. The 13th's own remedy (make it one source) applies here too.

summary: 1 critical, 1 medium, 2 low, 3 info. The critical one blocks: a plain-notation, no-encoding, no-substitution class — shell metacharacters welded to the verb or the operand — returns allow (auto-approved, no prompt) for the whole control plane including the plugin install root, and for Layer 1's deny tier as well; deletion verified in bash and zsh. Pre-existing across the entire F65 cycle and not covered by any declared residual axis. The single-source verb structure, the self-referencing-local class, the Layer 1/2 division of labour, and the .claude/ recovery-plane claim all check out.
